name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that dual service in legislative and executive departments violates separation of powers, but the specific employments in this case with NSHE and local government do not constitute such a violation.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the district court violated the principle of party presentation and that the majority's analysis of the separation-of-powers issue was procedurally and substantively flawed, requiring reversal and remand for further factual development.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NSHE should be considered part of the executive branch and that the majority's analysis for Neal, Torres, and Miller was incorrect, requiring further factual development. Concurred that Ohrenschall's dual service was compatible.

name: LEE, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority oversimplified the separation-of-powers issue by focusing on the department rather than the individual's specific functions, siding with Justice Herndon for reversal and remand. Concurred on party presentation and ancillary issues.

name: Pickering, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Nevada Constitution allows a regulated public utility to exercise delegated eminent domain power for a statutorily recognized public use, and a jury determination of public use is not required without genuine issues of material fact.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the terms used in the statutes have ordinary meanings and industry usage that provide sufficient clarity, and that the statutes are general intent statutes with an implicit scienter requirement, thus not unconstitutionally vague.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the initiative petition met the single-subject requirement as all provisions relate to reproductive freedom, the description of effect was legally sufficient, and it did not require an expenditure of money.

name: CADISH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the prosecutorial-consent requirement for informal supervision is not a sentencing decision and therefore does not violate the separation of powers doctrine.

name: STIGLICH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that both the governor and the chief justice have complementary constitutional authority to designate temporary substitutes for disqualified justices, and the chief justice's assignments were permissible.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred that both the governor and chief justice have appointment powers, but dissented from the majority's endorsement of a disparate, discretionary approach to judicial selection, arguing that the method should be random and uniform to maintain public trust.

name: Honorable Elissa F. Cadish
description: Disqualified from participating in the resolution of the objection and motion.

name: Honorable Patricia Lee
description: Disqualified from participating in the resolution of the objection and motion.

name: Honorable Michael Cherry
description: Did not participate in the resolution of the objection and motion.

name: Honorable Abbi Silver
description: Did not participate in the resolution of the objection and motion.

name: CAD1SH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that a private right of action for money damages exists for search-and-seizure violations under the Nevada Constitution, and qualified immunity does not apply.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the district court properly enjoined the initiative because it was an unfunded mandate, had a misleading description of effect, and impaired the Legislature's deliberative function.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the initiative was valid because the funding mandate does not apply to constitutional amendments, the description of effect was adequate, and initiatives can direct the Legislature to enact laws.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the initiative was valid because the funding mandate does not apply to constitutional amendments, the description of effect was adequate, and initiatives can direct the Legislature to enact laws.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that NRS 295.026 is a constitutional exercise of legislative power that facilitates the people's initiative power, and withdrawn petitions are void, nullifying the Secretary of State's duty to place them on the ballot.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that NRS 295.026 obstructs the Secretary of State's constitutional duty to place verified initiative petitions on the ballot after legislative inaction, and therefore should be held unconstitutional.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Dissented, agreeing with Justice Hardesty's opinion that NRS 295.026 obstructs the constitutional process.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, agreeing with Justice Hardesty's opinion that NRS 295.026 obstructs the constitutional process.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Nevada Constitution textually commits broad, discretionary authority over public education, including funding, to the Legislature, making the claims nonjusticiable political questions.

name: CADISH, J.
description: Dissented, argued that education is a fundamental right imposing a judicially enforceable, mandatory duty on the Legislature to provide a basic education, and therefore the issue is not a nonjusticiable political question.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Nevada Constitution's separation of powers clause prohibits a legislator from simultaneously serving as a prosecutor, and the court should have addressed the merits of the challenge and determined an appropriate remedy.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's focus solely on the petitioner's requested remedy was shortsighted and ignored the constitutional issue, which warrants extraordinary relief to protect the integrity of the judicial process.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, agreed with the opinions of Justice Silver and Justice Herndon.

name: CADISH, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that public policy does not support a forfeiture exception to the homestead exemption and that incarceration is a temporary absence that does not negate residency for homestead purposes.

name: HARDESTY, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion that expanded the public-importance exception to standing for separation-of-powers challenges that are likely to recur and require future guidance, even if they do not involve legislative expenditures.

name: HARDESTY, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the district court erred by broadly interpreting 'victim' under Marsy's Law and NRS 176.015(5)(d) to include anyone impacted by the crime, and by failing to determine the relevance and reliability of non-victim statements, thus requiring vacation of the sentence and remand for resentencing.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that employee status for MWA claims is determined by the economic realities test, and for NRS Chapter 608 claims, NRS 608.0155 may apply; contractual disavowals and NTA approval are not conclusive for either.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority opinion does not preclude waiting time penalties as a remedy under the MWA's 'all remedies' clause when sought as part of a constitutional violation.

name: SILVER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that general tailoring arguments are impermissible under Nevada's Constitution, but the error in this specific case was harmless.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, agreeing that general tailoring arguments are impermissible under Nevada's Constitution.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the federal economic realities test applies to define "employee" under the MWA, finding the Doe Dancers are employees, and NRS 608.0155 cannot abrogate these constitutional protections.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the Legislature intended NRS 608.0155 to limit the MWA's scope, it lacked the constitutional power to do so, and disagreed with some facts used to determine the employment relationship.
